For the testable checkpoints, the Router was not too lenient; the parabolic curve, feed horn assembly, and mount structure are all clearly visible and conform to the taxonomy of a radio telescope. The classification of the surface as 'solid aluminum panels' is reasonable given the smooth white appearance, though mesh is also possible at this resolution.
artifact_review: The Router identified low-severity texture anomalies and blur, attributing them to compression/resolution. The Perceptual Quality Auditor confirmed 'compression' artifacts with moderate severity. The Geometric Depth Auditor found no spatial warping or grounding failures, which is critical for a rigid mechanical structure like a telescope. The Topology Boundary Auditor reported high confidence (0.9894) in the mask for the sub-reflector struts, suggesting they are well-connected and not floating—a common AI failure mode that was successfully avoided here. I agree with the Router's assessment that there are no catastrophic structural artifacts, only minor quality degradations typical of lower-resolution inputs.

The complex truss work and thin support struts are coherent and do not exhibit melting, fusion, or topological fragmentation. The artifact score is penalized for the visual noise/compression but rewarded for the absence of generative structural failures.
